findings.desc: CHK-001:adversarial:1 claims evidence proves "Peer with parallelSafe=no has overlapping path -> no overlap_declared_parallel block (peer must also assert parallel)," but the smoke block 8 (line 142-151 of parallel-decomposition-gate-smoke.ts) tests the CONVERSE scenario: story parallelSafe=no with a parallel peer. No smoke fixture exercises story=parallel + peer=non-parallel + overlapping paths. The gate code at line 73 does implement this correctly (assertsParallel(peer) check), but the smoke evidence does not directly assert the stated claim. CHK-002:edge:4 claims the same scenario is covered by the smoke, compounding the mismatch.

CHK-001:adversarial:2 claims evidence proves "Story own contract missing from Map -> fail-open (block=null, NOT peer_contract_unreadable)." No smoke block omits the story S from the contracts Map. Every fixture in parallel-decomposition-gate-smoke.ts (blocks 1-10) passes a contract for story S. The gate implementation at lines 62-63 handles this correctly (sContract check, sWriteSet defaults to []), but the stated behavioral claim is never exercised by the smoke. The evidence command node packages/main/dist/tasks/parallel-decomposition-gate-smoke.js does not cover this intent.

CHK-001:adversarial:3 claims evidence proves "Multiple peers: one DONE (ignored), one active with overlap, one active with missing contract -> block=overlap_declared_parallel (highest precedence)." No single smoke fixture combines all three conditions: a DONE peer (filtered), an active parallel peer with a literal collision, AND an active parallel peer with no contract. The three conditions are each proven in isolation (blocks 7, 2, 5 respectively) but never simultaneously, so the multi-peer precedence interaction with mixed terminal/active peers is not exercised. CHK-002:adversarial:1 also claims "overlap > peer_contract_unreadable > broad_glob" three-way precedence is asserted, but no fixture combines all three firing conditions simultaneously; only overlap > broad is tested (smoke block 9, line 162).

CHK-001:edge:0 and CHK-001:edge:1 claim separate evidence for DONE filtering and DISCARDED filtering respectively, but smoke block 7 (lines 127-139 of parallel-decomposition-gate-smoke.ts) tests BOTH terminal phases in a single fixture by passing both a DONE peer and a DISCARDED peer simultaneously. A single assertion (block null) cannot distinguish which filtering rule is responsible for the result. If DONE filtering were silently broken but DISCARDED filtering were correct, the block-7 assertion would still pass because the DISCARDED peer is also excluded. The two intents are not independently falsifiable by the current evidence.

dead code: parallel-policy.ts:34-45 JSDoc for resolveParallelSafety is now orphaned — TERMINAL_PHASES insertion placed a second JSDoc block between the existing comment and the function, so resolveParallelSafety has no attached doc and the older JSDoc block is unreachable dead comment
dead code: parallel-decomposition-gate-smoke.ts:45 uses async IIFE (void (async () => {) with no await expression inside; the async keyword is unnecessary dead modifier

CHK-001:adversarial:4 intent claims block=null with EMPTY advisories when all supplied peers are terminal (DONE/DISCARDED) and story has a broad glob. Smoke block-5 (lines 97-107) tests peers=[] (truly no peers, not all-terminal) and checks that a broad advisory IS emitted. Smoke block-10/11 (lines 164-171) tests isolated DONE/DISCARDED peers but uses a literal-collision contract (not broad), and asserts only block=null without touching advisories. Neither block covers the exact scenario: (a) non-empty peer list where every peer is DONE/DISCARDED, (b) broad-glob story, (c) advisories is empty. The evidence command node packages/main/dist/tasks/parallel-decomposition-gate-smoke.js correctly points to the smoke, but the smoke does not assert the three-way conjunction required by this intent.
